title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues §3 of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' (ms. p. 662, archive p. 663). The setting is a profinite 'modular' situation.

Objects (from the preceding pages):
- 𝔖⁺ is a profinite group, e.g. a subgroup of SL(2,Ẑ) or a variant of it. It carries two distinguished elements, ρ of order 3 and σ of order 2.
- 𝔖^𝔖 is a subgroup of 𝔖⁺.
- L_0 is a procyclic 'cusp' (loop) subgroup topologically generated by ξ_0, the parabolic/inertia element at infinity, with L_0^𝔖 = L_0 ∩ 𝔖^𝔖.
- G^𝔖_{ρ,σ} is a group of 'rigidified' automorphism data. It is built from Z_{ρσ}: systems u = (u, μ, ε₃, ε₂), where u is an automorphism, μ ∈ Ẑ* is a cyclotomic character and ε₃, ε₂ ∈ μ = {±1}. These are subject to conjugacy conditions on ρ, σ and L_0, in the spirit of the definition of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group by its action on the generators of the modular group.
- (45) is the homomorphism G^𝔖_{ρ,σ} → Aut(𝔖⁺)×μ×μ, u ↦ (int(u)|𝔖⁺, ε₃(u), ε₂(u)). Its image is described by conditions (46) and its kernel by (47).
- (48) defines SN_0 = Norm_{𝔖⁺}(L_0) and SN_0^𝔖 = SN_0 ∩ 𝔖^𝔖.
- (49) defines the extended normaliser SÑ_0^𝔖 of pairs (f, μ) with int(f)(ξ_0) = ξ_0^μ. So μ is the 'cyclotomic' exponent by which f acts on the cusp generator.
- (50) says the projection SÑ_0^𝔖 → SN_0^𝔖 is an isomorphism when n ↦ ξ_0^n, Ẑ → L_0^𝔖, is injective.
- (51) is a canonical injective homomorphism SÑ_0^𝔖 → S_0G^𝔖_{ρ,σ} = Z_{ρ,σ}·𝔖⁺, (f, μ) ↦ f⁻¹·(int(f), μ, 1, 1).

What this page states:
- The map (51) induces on L_0^𝔖 the canonical homomorphism (28) and extends (42).
- The inverse image of i_{L_0,𝔖}(L_0^𝔖) is exactly L_0^𝔖 ⊂ SÑ_0^𝔖.
- Combining with (45)–(47), one gets a canonical four-term exact sequence (52):
  1 → L_0^𝔖 → SÑ_0^𝔖 → G^𝔖_{ρ,σ} → G̃̃_{ρ,σ} → 1,
  where G̃̃_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Aut(𝔖⁺)×μ×μ is the image of (45), i.e. the triples (u, ε₃, ε₂) satisfying (46).
- Equivalently, (52 bis): SÑ_0^𝔖 / L_0^𝔖 ≅ Ker(G^𝔖_{ρ,σ} → Aut(𝔖⁺)×μ×μ).

In words: the 'inner' part of the rigidified automorphism group is the normaliser of the cusp group, with its cyclotomic twist, taken modulo the cusp group itself. This is the familiar pattern 'normaliser mod subgroup = automorphisms fixing the extra structure that are inner'. It is a profinite, Teichmüller-tower analogue of computing the stabiliser of a marked cusp in the modular group.

Role in the larger work: the page is part of a systematic dévissage of the groups G_{ρ,σ}. The next page goes on to the analogous normalisers and centralisers N_ρ, N_σ, Z_ρ, Z_σ, with the sequences 1 → Z → N → μ → 1 split by τ'. These computations feed the study of the 'loop equation', i.e. the relations defining GT-type groups acting on the modular tower.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The claim that the inverse image of i_{L_0,𝔖}(L_0^𝔖) is exactly L_0^𝔖 is asserted ('il est encore vrai') without proof. It depends on the injectivity of (51) and on hypothesis (50), namely that Ẑ → L_0^𝔖 is injective, which is not restated here.
The definition of G̃̃_{ρ,σ} is left unfinished ('i.e. ...'). Its characterisation is implicitly the image description (46) from the previous page.
The ordering of the signs (ε₂, ε₃) on this page appears to be swapped relative to (45), which uses (ε₃, ε₂). This is a harmless notational inconsistency.

ideas.what: Four-term exact sequence relating the cusp subgroup L_0, its extended (cyclotomic) normaliser, the rigidified automorphism group G_{ρ,σ}, and its image in Aut(𝔖⁺)×μ×μ
ideas.modern_name: Exact sequence 'inner automorphisms = normaliser/centraliser'; stabiliser of a cusp with Galois-twisted action (Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type automorphism groups of profinite modular groups)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group theory; the GT setting is due to Drinfeld and Ihara and to work on GT acting on profinite SL2/PSL2 (e.g. Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura)
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished notes (archive cote 140-3). The general program is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche.

ideas.what: Extended normaliser SÑ_0 = {(f, μ) : f ξ_0 f⁻¹ = ξ_0^μ}, recording the cyclotomic exponent on the cusp generator
ideas.modern_name: Normaliser of inertia (cusp) subgroup with cyclotomic character; 'tangential base point' rigidification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in anabelian geometry (Deligne's tangential base points; Ihara; Nakamura)
ideas.where_published: Ideas of this kind circulate in La Longue Marche (1981); the exact formulation here is unsure.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine bookkeeping page: a standard exact sequence identifying the kernel of the map to outer data with the cusp normaliser modulo the cusp group. It belongs to a long dévissage, and the thread itself is unfinished ('i.e. ...'). There is no independent new result on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'G_{g,σ}' should read G_{ρ,σ}; the subscript is ρ, as in (45) on the previous page.
'satisfaisant (??σ)' most likely reads 'satisfaisant (46)', referring to the image conditions of the previous page.
The superscript '(28)' above 'canonique' is an inserted reference: 'l'hom canonique (28)'.
The struck-out words before G̃̃_{ρ,σ} are illegible deletions; the line reads 'où G̃̃_{ρ,σ} est formé des (u, ε₂, ε₃) satisfaisant (46)'. The letters are epsilons (signs), not ξ.
'(52 bis)' is correct; the main sequence is numbered (52) ('(5?)' in the image).
